newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda details January coffee sales.
newsitem.headline: Uganda details January coffee sales.

text.p: Coffee sales in Uganda were marginally higher in January compared with December, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Wednesday.
Sales totalled 551,688 60-kg bags valued at $38.56 million, versus 514,394 bags worth $35.85 million in December, the UCDA said in a report.
Compared with January last year, the volume and value of exports fell by 0.15 percent and 23.2 percent respectively.
Robustas realised a unit value of $1.07 in January 1997 down form $1.27 in January 1996.
But the unit value of arabicas rose to $2.02 per kg from $1.75 in January last year -- reflecting supply tightness in arabicas and a surplus in robustas.

In the first four months of the 1996/97 season, cumulative exports amounted to 1,842,784 bags valued at $133.8 million against 1,348,034 60-kilo bags valued at $138.2 million in the same period last season, UCDA said.
The UCDA attributed the rise in volume to the high level of closing stocks at the end of 1995/96 and a heavy harvest in central and eastern regions.
Exporters took advantage of high availability to fill contracts pending from 1995/96.
Also, farmers and processors might have been front-loading their stocks onto the market as quickly as possible to avoid financial losses, UCDA said.
Locally, prices paid to farmers rose from an average of 350 shillings per kg of kiboko in December 1996 to 500-600 shillings from the third week of January.
Prices of Fair Average Quality (FAQ) ranged between 1,100 and 1,200 and arabica parchment between 1,300 and 1,400.
Average export prices reflected the international market, rising to mid-January levels of $1.32 from $1.21 in December 1996.
More than 80 percent of exports were handled by 14 exporters, with Nsamba Coffee Works Ltd topping the list with 14.50 percent.
By end-January, 53 exporters had been licensed to operate in 1996/97.
